correctness.rationale: For B>=0 with B<=qI, B²<=qB. Restricting a test vector to at most m-1 positions and lower-bounding the remaining m-k coordinates gives h<= q s/(s²+m-k), whose maximum is <=q sqrt(m-1)/m. Rank-one block B=q J_m/m attains equality. Keeping the first entry strictly above m-th tail guarantees survival, while a tail-to-leading ratio contracts by q each update. The exact counterexample at and below the boundary is an absorbing wrong-eigenvector state. Exact fraction and randomized tests are supplementary, not infinite verification.

value.rationale: This exact support-retention frontier resolves a genuine failure mode of hard-thresholded eigensolvers: even an exact one-sparse dominant eigenvector can be irretrievably discarded by a single iteration despite nonzero initial overlap. The full sharp m- and q-dependent threshold, all-iteration guarantee and rank-one PSD trapping family together provide meaningful structural insight beyond a routine lemma or isolated finite counterexample.
